stages.name: Fraudulent GTA VI Storefronts
observables: Domains containing 'cyberleek'
Impersonation of Rockstar Games, PlayStation, or Xbox storefronts
Promotion of a non-existent PC version or beta
Requests for cryptocurrency payments ($CYBERLEEK/SOL)

stages.name: Malicious Installer Delivery
observables: gta6_installer.exe
Executable size of approximately 1.1 MB
GTA VI-themed ISO disk image files
Fake 'Play Now' buttons on cloned sites

stages.name: Fake Installer Execution
observables: Execution of gta6_installer.exe
Mounting of malicious ISO images
Execution of Vidar infostealer or remote-access trojans

stages.name: Credential and Wallet Harvesting
observables: Access to Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Brave, Opera, and Vivaldi profile directories
Extraction of saved browser passwords and autofill data
Stealing of FTP credentials
Accessing cryptocurrency wallet data

stages.name: Command and Control via Multi-hop Proxy
observables: Outbound connections to multi-hop proxy nodes
Chained proxy traffic to mask C2 origin
Communication with CyberLeek-linked infrastructure

stages.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
observables: Rapid encryption of user files
Massive file renaming or modification activity
Creation of ransom notes on the desktop or in user folders

scenario.summary: Adversaries leverage extreme hype for Grand Theft Auto VI to distribute Vidar infostealers, remote-access trojans, and ransomware via fake 'early access' storefronts and malicious installers. These campaigns target browser credentials, crypto wallets, and local files, often using the 'CyberLeek' brand and associated cryptocurrency lures to trick fans into executing malicious .exe or .iso payloads.

meta.rationale: The hunt starts with high-prevalence resolution data to find beachheads, then uses the 'cyberleek' string and explicit list as anchors to focus on affected hosts.
meta.hypothesis: The adversary exploits GTA VI anticipation by delivering Vidar infostealers through fraudulent storefronts and installers, identifiable by rare DNS resolutions and subsequent credential access from staging directories.

hunt.name: GTA VI Fake Installer and Phishing Scams
hunt.description: The adversary uses the hype around GTA VI to lure victims into interacting with malicious storefronts and downloading fake installers. The hunt identifies hosts resolving CyberLeek-linked domains or rare infrastructure, then pivots to examine file creation in user-writable directories. Finally, the hunt correlates these drops with unauthorized processes attempting to harvest browser credentials, confirming a Vidar infection.

nodes.label: Lead: DNS resolutions for scam infrastructure

config.content: WITH target_hosts AS (SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE (LOWER(query_hostname) LIKE '%cyberleek%' OR instr(',' || '{{scam_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')) SELECT d.device_hostname, d.query_hostname, d.time FROM hb_dns_activity d INNER JOIN target_hosts h ON d.device_hostname = h.device_hostname WHERE d.time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY 1, 2 HAVING (LOWER(d.query_hostname) LIKE '%cyberleek%' OR instr(',' || '{{scam_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(d.query_hostname) || ',') > 0 OR COUNT(DISTINCT d.device_hostname) < 3)
config.description: Identify hosts resolving domains associated with the CyberLeek campaign or fraudulent GTA VI offers, including rare infrastructure seen on those same hosts.
config.expected_signal: A list of hostnames and the domains they resolved. Any resolution of a known scam domain or a rare domain on a suspicious host is a hit.

config.objective: Determine if the DNS resolutions in dns-scam-leads indicate interaction with scam storefronts or potential malware command-and-control.
config.description: Assess the initial DNS leads to decide if full forensic queries are justified.
config.expected_signal: A per-host verdict on whether the DNS activity is likely a scam interaction.

nodes.label: Rare files created in staging directories

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, file_path, file_name, time, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) as fleet_hosts FROM hb_file_activity WHERE ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND (LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\\downloads\\%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\\temp\\%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\\users\\public\\%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 HAVING fleet_hosts < 3
config.description: Locate rare files dropped in common user-writable directories, which often precede installer execution.
config.expected_signal: Creation of an installer or ISO in a staging folder that appears on very few hosts. Silence in the 10-minute window of the DNS lead suggests no drop occurred.

nodes.label: Credential store access from staging processes

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, file_path, file_name, time FROM hb_file_activity WHERE ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND activity_id = 2 AND LOWER(file_name) IN ('login data', 'cookies', 'web data') AND (LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\\downloads\\%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\\temp\\%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\\users\\public\\%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify non-browser processes launched from staging paths that read sensitive browser files, a core Vidar infostealer behavior.
config.expected_signal: Rows showing a process in a temp/download folder reading Chrome or Edge profile data. This is high-confidence evidence of infostealer execution.
